clue.text: City foremost in commerce one holding record

indicators.note: foremost in points to the leading letter of the word commerce
holding says the word for one wraps around the record

parts.note: taken as the word written out
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A city that leads in trade and is the one holding some record or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is not I here but the word ONE itself, opened up to take LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne is a large German city on the Rhine.

clue.text: Crush nut noisily

indicators.note: noisily says the word for the nut is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a conker is the nut of the horse chestnut tree, used in a British children's game

explanation.surface: An instruction to crack a nut loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: CONKERS is a British schoolyard game played with horse chestnuts on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush an enemy is to defeat or subdue them utterly.

clue.text: Knowledge passed down about current in continental river

indicators.note: about means the traditional knowledge goes around the current symbol

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge handed down through generations
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Folk wisdom handed down about the current in some river in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, on the European continent.

clue.text: Fabric, mostly repulsive, with appearance of wood

indicators.note: mostly means the word for repulsive loses its final letter

parts.note: gross means disgusting or repulsive
grain is the pattern of fibres visible in wood

explanation.surface: A cloth, rather ugly, made to look like timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Grosgrain is a heavy ribbed silk or rayon cloth, often used for ribbons.

clue.text: Unruly geezer once sober causes misery

definitions.note: in British slang a misery is a gloomy, complaining person, an old grouch

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowdy bloke who used to be teetotal now makes everyone unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causes' looks like part of the definition but is only a link. A geezer is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's miser in A Christmas Carol is the archetypal grouch, a byword for a killjoy.

clue.text: Champions' anthem approximately reproduced in chant of 10 18 9 1A?

indicators.note: a crowd chanting these grid words roughly produces the song's title, so they are said aloud

parts.note: the answers to 10 across, 18 down, 9 across and 1 across, chanted in that order

explanation.surface: A football song is roughly what you get when you chant four other answers in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: Chanting YULE NAVARRE WALL COLOGNE comes out roughly as the song title. Champions are Liverpool, European champions, whose fans sing it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rodgers and Hammerstein song from Carousel is the anthem sung by Liverpool fans.

clue.text: Two articles written to support Yankee in Chinese city

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pieces written beneath the other hold it up from below

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
two copies of the indefinite article an

explanation.surface: A pair of newspaper pieces written backing an American in a city in China.
explanation.definitionFit: Yan'an in Shaanxi province is the Chinese city where Mao's Long March ended.

clue.text: Lacking packing? Not carried away we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase for not carried away is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: rapt means carried away with delight, so un-rapt means not carried away

explanation.surface: Something without its wrapping, calmly described as not swept off its feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel with its paper taken off has no packing round it.

clue.text: Records suppressing previous signs of inexperience

indicators.note: suppressing says the records hold down the word for previous, keeping it within

parts.note: LPs are long-playing vinyl records
late means former or previous, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: Old records that hide earlier marks of a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates are the red L signs British learner drivers must display.
explanation.definitionFit: Learner plates mark a driver still in training, a beginner.

clue.text: Maori perhaps sees a ridiculous point made by churchman

indicators.note: ridiculous means absurd, so the letters of point are made nonsense of and rearranged

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman in charge of a cathedral

explanation.surface: A New Zealander watches a cleric make a silly argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maori is from New Zealand, which Britons call the Antipodes, being on the far side of the globe.

clue.text: Lehman Brothers went to this wealthy Manhattan street

definitions.meaning: to go to the ... is to collapse into bankruptcy, as the bank did in 2008
the New York financial district street, home of the stock exchange

explanation.surface: The failed bank ended up at the rich New York thoroughfare.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the wall is an idiom for business failure; Wall Street is the financial heart of Manhattan.

clue.text: Brynner Theatre's closing for the festive season

parts.note: Yul Brynner was the actor famed for The King and I

indicators.note: closing points to the final letter of the word Theatre's

explanation.surface: An actor's theatre shuts for Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is an old name for the Christmas period.

clue.text: Organisation that takes role in energy recycling?

indicators.note: takes means the shuffled letters admit the word for role into their midst
recycling means the letters of energy are reprocessed into a new order

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A body that plays its part in recycling energy, as an environmental movement might.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes an eco-friendly political body, so it reads almost as a definition throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: The environmentalist political group is a kind of organisation.

clue.text: Beer has bit of a head — dash round?

parts.note: the brow is the forehead, part of the head

indicators.note: round means the word for dash is turned about, read backwards

parts.note: elan means dash or panache

explanation.surface: A beer with some foam on top, to be swigged quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown ale is a dark, sweetish British bottled beer.

clue.text: See 5
Sack belonging to French model

parts.note: de is French for of, showing belonging
to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: Dismiss a French fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a ruler is to remove or oust them from office.

clue.text: Determined a number climbing in fell

indicators.note: in places the upturned pieces inside the word for fell

parts.note: died means fell, as soldiers fall in battle

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word for number is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: a song is a musical number

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to climb a mountain with a tune in their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a hill to climb but is the verb for perishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who has determined the illness has identified its cause.

clue.text: Everyone in Slough is degenerate

indicators.note: in puts the word for everyone within the marshland

parts.note: a slough is a swamp, and a fen is marshy ground
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A jibe that the whole town of Slough is decadent.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the English town west of London but is the bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallen person has sunk morally, become corrupt or debased.

clue.text: Enduring wobbly sea-legs

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone still unsteady on board ship, sea-legs not yet found.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timeless never grows old, so it lasts on and on.

clue.text: Substitute with good reputation

parts.note: a stand-in is a substitute

explanation.surface: A replacement player who is well thought of.
explanation.definitionFit: One's standing is one's status or esteem in the eyes of others.

clue.text: Welshman going north has arrived in Pamplona area

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for arrived within the upturned name
in a down clue going north means the name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh man's name
arr is the timetable abbreviation for arrived

explanation.surface: A Welsh traveller heading north reaches the Spanish city of the bull run.
explanation.definitionFit: Navarre is the Spanish region whose capital is Pamplona.

clue.text: Solid figure reached out into river

indicators.note: into puts the shuffled letters inside the river's name

parts.note: the Don is a river in Russia and in Yorkshire

indicators.note: out means the letters of reached are put out of order

explanation.surface: A geometric shape that someone stretched out over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A decahedron is a polyhedron with ten faces.

clue.text: Do well with fish — ten about to be netted

indicators.note: to be netted means the next pieces are caught inside the fish

parts.note: an eel is a fish
X is the Roman numeral ten
c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Succeed at fishing, landing ten or so in the net.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to perform outstandingly, to shine.

clue.text: Rotter does away with king in cathedral area

indicators.note: does away with means the king's letter is removed from the rogue

parts.note: a knave is a scoundrel or rotter
K is king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A scoundrel murders a king inside a cathedral, as with Becket.
explanation.definitionFit: The nave is the main central body of a church where the congregation sits.

clue.text: See 5
Volume increase at the end almost closed bar

indicators.note: at the end points to the last letter of the word increase

parts.note: a door that is to is pushed nearly shut

explanation.surface: Turning the music up at closing time in a pub that has nearly shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the verb meaning to forbid.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto something is to forbid or block it.

clue.text: Angry about southern musical styles

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry
over means about, as in a row over money

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by music from the South.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossover music blends genres, such as classical with pop.

clue.text: Lift small duck

parts.note: a teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: Pick up a little duck.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is slang for pinching or stealing it.

clue.text: Sign used by vendors everywhere

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A notice that street traders everywhere put up.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a cheque is to put one's signature on the back of it.
